media_work.title: An Unreal Dream: The Michael Morton Story
media_work.publisher_or_network: Blue Bandana Productions, Glass House Productions, La Sonrisa Productions Inc. (A CNN Films documentary)
media_work.focus_or_theme: The wrongful conviction of Michael Morton for the 1986 murder of his wife, Christine, in Texas. Chronicles his nearly 25 years in prison and his eventual exoneration through DNA testing, highlighting severe prosecutorial misconduct.
media_work.summaryNotes: Morton served nearly 25 years before being exonerated by DNA in 2011. His case led to the passage of the Michael Morton Act in Texas, reforming discovery laws.

media_item.item_title: An Unreal Dream: The Michael Morton Story
media_item.focus_or_theme: The wrongful conviction of Michael Morton for the 1986 murder of his wife, Christine, in Texas. Chronicles his nearly 25 years in prison and his eventual exoneration through DNA testing, highlighting severe prosecutorial misconduct.
media_item.summary_notes: Chronicles Michael Morton's wrongful conviction for the murder of his wife, his nearly 25 years in prison, and his eventual exoneration through DNA testing. The documentary highlights severe prosecutorial misconduct and the impact on Morton's relationship with his son.
key_quotes_raw: Interviews with Michael Morton reflecting on his experience
Attorney John Raley discussing the legal fight
Discussion of the impact on Morton's relationship with his son
Quote often associated with the title/case (from Judge Learned Hand): "'Our procedure has been always haunted by the ghost of the innocent man convicted. It is an unreal dream.'"
systemic_issues_raw: Prosecutorial misconduct (Brady violations) and lack of accountability
Challenges in obtaining post-conviction DNA testing
The devastating personal cost of wrongful imprisonment
policy_recommendations_raw: Highlights the need for stronger enforcement against prosecutorial misconduct
Supports reforms like the Michael Morton Act mandating open-file discovery in Texas criminal cases

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Murder of his wife, Christine Morton
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Wrongfully convicted of the murder of his wife, Christine Morton, in Williamson County, Texas. He served nearly 25 years in prison before being exonerated in 2011 through DNA testing. The case involved prosecutorial misconduct and flawed investigation.
contributing_factors_raw: Prosecutorial misconduct (deliberate withholding of exculpatory evidence, including police reports indicating another man might be responsible, witness statements, and notes about his son witnessing the attack by a "monster")
